description: Fix the non-functional /logs page end-to-end: make the server write real structured (NDJSON) file logs to the advertised ~/.mohist/logs location, replace the ad-hoc /api/logs/tail response with one typed contract both sides honor (structured per-line element, incremental cursor, source identity, truncation/reset, and an explicit source-unavailable state), and make the Web page source-aware so it renders the real File: line and an actionable unavailable diagnostic instead of a bare 'No logs available'.

tasks.title: Server file logging: write real NDJSON logs to a redirectable ~/.mohist/logs
tasks.spec: specs/server-file-logging/spec.md#Server daemon writes structured JSON file logs
tasks.description: Introduce ILogPathResolver (honors a Mohist:LogsPath config override, falls back to HOME/.mohist/logs) as the single path source consumed by the file logger, the tail endpoint, and SystemInfoService. Rewire SystemInfoService.ResolvePaths() Logs field off the resolver so the advertised path and the real path cannot drift. Update the integration fixture to redirect Mohist:LogsPath to a per-run temp dir (cleaned up on dispose). Add a custom FileLoggerProvider + FileLogger under src/Mohist.Server/Logging/ that appends one JSON object per line (matching the agreed LogRecord shape: level/time/service/message + exception) to {resolved}/server.log via FileShare.ReadWrite, creating the directory on first write, using the injected TimeProvider and JSON.Options. Register AddFileLogger in Program.cs on BOTH the primary host and the BuildAlternateApp fallback path so OTLP-bind-failure recovery logs identically.
acceptanceCriteria: ILogPathResolver is registered in DI and resolves Mohist:LogsPath when set, otherwise HOME/.mohist/logs (identical to today's inline computation).

SystemInfoService.ResolvePaths() sources its Logs path from ILogPathResolver instead of computing Path.Combine(home, ".mohist", "logs") inline; the advertised SystemPaths.Logs value is unchanged for the default case.
The integration fixture sets Mohist:LogsPath to a per-run temp directory in ConfigureWebHost and deletes it in DisposeAsync, so server specs never touch the real ~/.mohist/logs.
FileLoggerProvider appends one JSON object per physical line to {logDir}/server.log; each written record contains level, time, service, and message fields (plus exception/fields when present).
The log directory is created by the provider before the first record is written when it does not exist.
Records are appended across the daemon lifetime and the file remains concurrently readable (opened with FileShare.ReadWrite) by the tail reader.
AddFileLogger is registered in Program.cs on both the primary builder and the BuildAlternateApp path.

A unit test asserts a record written by FileLoggerProvider parses into the agreed element shape with level/time/service/message populated (no field loss), serializing through JSON.Options so the format matches the API pipeline.
npm test (server) passes with the new tests included.
tasks.output: src/Mohist.Server/Logging/ (ILogPathResolver, LogPathResolver, FileLoggerProvider, FileLogger, LogRecord); updated SystemInfoService.cs, MohistServiceRegistration.cs, Program.cs, MohistIntegrationFixture.cs; passing server unit tests for the provider and resolver.
tasks.notes: Per design D2/D3: zero new external packages — a custom ILoggerProvider (~120 LOC) in the existing Microsoft.Extensions.Logging pipeline gives exact control over the NDJSON shape so it matches the tail contract by construction. LogRecord fields (level/time/service/message) are the single per-line element type used end-to-end; T-002 defines the tail-facing LogEntry (= LogRecord fields + raw) and depends on this format.

tasks.title: Typed /api/logs/tail contract: agreed shape, unavailable state, reset/truncation, source identity
tasks.description: Rewrite GET /api/logs/tail to return one always-present typed response: lines (structured LogEntry[]), cursor/nextCursor (byte offset), source (file name), truncated, reset, unavailable, expectedLocation, reason. Consume ILogPathResolver (from T-001) and read server.log directly (newest *.log only as a transitional discovery fallback). Project each NDJSON line into LogEntry (level/time/service/message + raw = original line); degrade non-JSON lines to an element with message=raw and null level/time/service. Compute reset=true on first read (no cursor) or when the file shrank below the cursor (rotation/truncation, restarting from byte 0); truncated=true when the line/byte cap hit before EOF. When the log directory or file is absent, return unavailable=true with expectedLocation (resolved path) and a human-readable reason, distinct from an available source that returned zero new lines. Add LogsRouteSpecs at the API boundary covering all paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Every /api/logs/tail response (with or without cursor, available or unavailable) includes lines, cursor, nextCursor, source, truncated, reset, unavailable, expectedLocation, and reason — no field the page depends on is undefined.
Each lines element is the structured LogEntry type (level/time/service/message/raw); the server never emits raw JSON strings for the client to parse, so no client-side JSON.parse is needed.
A non-JSON line degrades to an element of the same type whose message is the raw line and whose level/time/service are null; no raw string is mixed into the element list.
Passing the cursor back yields only lines after the previous read and returns an updated nextCursor (incremental byte-offset tailing preserved).
source reflects the active log file name (server.log) so the Web can render it as the File: line.

truncated=true when the line-count or byte cap is reached before EOF; reset=true on a first read (no cursor) and when the source rotated/truncated (file length < cursor), causing the client to replace its view.

When the expected log directory/file is missing, the response reports unavailable=true with the expected log location path and a reason; when the source exists but has no new lines since the cursor, unavailable is false (available-but-empty is NOT reported as unavailable).

LogsRouteSpecs (via MohistIntegrationFixture) cover: the missing-directory/unavailable path (with expectedLocation), the agreed response shape, a populated tail (incremental cursor advance + truncation), the reset path (first read and/or rotation), and non-JSON line degradation.
A spec asserts a record written by the FileLoggerProvider (T-001) round-trips through the tail's LogEntry projection without field loss.
npm test (server) passes.
tasks.output: Rewritten Api/LogsRoutes.cs with LogEntry/response types (or a dedicated Logs contract file); new tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/.../LogsRouteSpecs.cs; passing server specs at the API boundary.
tasks.notes: Per design D1/D4/D5: single coordinated BREAKING change to /api/logs/tail is acceptable (the page is the only consumer; no runner/CLI usage). The wire field is nextCursor (server authority); the Web client stores it as its cursor (T-003). Keep FileShare.ReadWrite on the reader and the stateless byte-offset cursor model; rotation is detected by 'file shrank', needing no separate cursor store. The reader is stateless between requests.

tasks.title: Source-aware Logs page: consume agreed element type, render File: line and unavailable diagnostic
tasks.spec: specs/logs-page/spec.md#Web consumes the agreed line element type without double-parsing
tasks.description: Retype LogTailResult in pages/logs/model/api.ts to the agreed contract and export a LogEntry type. In useLogs.ts, delete parseLogLine and the JSON.parse double-parse; map result.lines straight into the entry list; expose source, unavailable, expectedLocation, reason, truncated, reset, and store nextCursor as the polling cursor. Make reset trigger view replacement (discard stale entries) and non-reset append (preserving the existing reset branch, which now actually works). In LogsPage.tsx, render File: {source} from the real source identity; replace the bare 'No logs available' empty state with two branches — an unavailable diagnostic (expected location + reason) when unavailable, and a neutral 'No matching logs' otherwise. Keep level filtering, search (across message/service/raw), export (emits each entry's raw joined by newlines), and auto-follow (polls with the incremental cursor, respects page visibility and pause-on-scroll-up) operating on the agreed element type. Add Web tests for useLogs and LogsPage.
acceptanceCriteria: LogTailResult in api.ts matches the agreed /api/logs/tail shape; a LogEntry type (level/time/service/message/raw) is exported.
useLogs consumes result.lines directly as structured elements and no longer runs JSON.parse on them, so level/time/service/message are preserved from the server elements (parseLogLine is deleted).
useLogs exposes source, unavailable, expectedLocation, reason, truncated, reset, and stores nextCursor as the cursor it passes back on the next poll.
reset causes useLogs to replace its entry view; non-reset appends new entries (preserving MAX_ENTRIES trimming and POLL_INTERVAL/visibility gating).
LogsPage renders the File: line from the real source identity returned by the API (no longer blank/undefined).

When the API reports unavailable, LogsPage renders an actionable diagnostic containing the expected log location and the reason, and does NOT render a bare 'No logs available'; when the source is available but the view is empty (no new lines or all filtered out), it does NOT show the unavailable diagnostic.
Level filtering, search, export (raw per entry), and auto-follow all operate against the agreed per-line element type and remain functional after the contract alignment.
Web tests cover: useLogs element preservation / reset replace-vs-append / unavailable passthrough, and LogsPage unavailable diagnostic vs. filtered-empty state plus the rendered File: source line.
npm run test:run -w packages/web and npm run typecheck -w packages/web pass.
tasks.output: Updated packages/web/src/pages/logs/model/api.ts, model/useLogs.ts, ui/LogsPage.tsx; new Web tests under pages/logs/; passing web typecheck and tests.
tasks.notes: Per design D6: parseLogLine is removed (keeping it as a defensive re-parse would reintroduce the double-parse bug). raw is retained on each element because export and search-across-original-text depend on it. Auto-follow polling parameters (MAX_ENTRIES, POLL_INTERVAL) and the visibility/scroll-up gating are unchanged; only the consumed element type and the cursor/reset/unavailable wiring change.
